answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every new worker to post a time-locked performance bond before it may submit work or grade peers. The bond stays frozen for a full cycle and is slashed if clustering or copy-paste answers reveal coordinated sockpuppets. Picture a hiring summit where access is priced in jade: each identity must lock 50 units for 14 days, about two weeks of expected pay. An attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must immobilize 50,000 units and wait out the lock; that capital cost drains the nectar of cheap identity farming.
